predecessors.name: Jurchen Confederation
predecessors.text: the Wanyan Jurchens' country round the Ashi river and Huanglong, subjects of the Khitan-led Liao until 1114

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: North China annexed by the Mongols with the fall of Caizhou on 9 February 1234 (Henan, Shaanxi and the remnant; Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong had passed to them by 1223)

ledger.x: 1115: Aguda proclaims the Jin.
1115: the war on the Liao holds ground.
1115: Huanglong falls to the Jin.
1120: the Supreme Capital is taken.
1122: the Central Capital falls.
1122: the Western Capital falls: 'the Jin took the Western Capital in the spring of 1122'.
1122: the Southern Capital falls: 'In the winter, Aguda took the Southern Capital'; the Wanyan Aguda page: 'between 1119 and 1122 his army captured all of the Liao dynasty's five capitals'.
1123: Yanjing and most of the Sixteen Prefectures pass to the Song.
1124: Western Xia becomes a Jin vassal.
1125: the Jin retake the Sixteen Prefectures 'in an invasion of Song territory in 1125'.
26 March 1125: the last Liao emperor is captured.
26 March 1125: the Liao conquest ends.
November 1125: the Jin invade the Song.
1126: Hebei and Shanxi pass to the Jin.
1126: the Jin hold Hebei and Shanxi; the war moves to the Yellow River.
1126: Goryeo submits.
9 January 1127: Kaifeng falls.
December 1129: two Jin armies cross the Huai; they seized Hangzhou on 22 January 1130 and Shaoxing on 4 February, then withdrew north.
1130: 'The Jurchens gave up the pursuit and retreated north'.
Late 1130: the Jin take the land north of the Qinling-Huai line.
Late 1130: the Jin make Liu Yu emperor of Qi on the plain.
1130: the Jin enthrone Liu Yu.
1136: the Jin cede the Qingtang area to Western Xia.
1137: Qi abolished.
1137: Jin rule replaces Qi on the plain.
1139: Henan and Shaanxi are returned to the Song.
1139: the Jin hand back Henan and Shaanxi.
1139: the Linxia and Lanzhou discs leave the Jin shape.
1140: the Jin retake the plain.
1140: Henan and Shaanxi are Jin again.
11 October 1142: the Treaty of Shaoxing.
1142: the Song renounce the north.
1142: the Song pay tribute.
1153: the capital moves to Zhongdu.
October 1161: Wanyan Liang crosses the Huai (28 October), loses at Tangdao (16 November) and Caishi (26-27 November) and is murdered on 15 December; Shizong was crowned at Liaoyang on 27 October.
1165: the Treaty of Longxing ends the war; the Jin-Song wars page: hostilities 'subsided in 1165 after the negotiation of a peace treaty'.
1165: the tribute lapses.
1206: the Song declare war (14 June 1206); 'by the fall of 1206, multiple towns and military bases had been captured by the Jurchens'.
2 November 1208: peace; the Song tribute to the Jin is reinstated (50,000 taels of silver and 50,000 packs of fabric).
1208: the Song are tributaries again ('the Song tribute to the Jin was reinstated').
1210: the Xia break with the Jin.
1211: the Mongols invade.
1212: the Khitans rebel.
27 June 1214: Xuanzong leaves Zhongdu for Bianjing (Kaifeng), 'above the objections of many courtiers'.
1215: Manchuria goes to Puxian Wannu.
1 June 1215: Zhongdu falls.
1223: the northern provinces are lost.
1231: Shaanxi is lost.
1233: the court flees to Caizhou.
1233: Kaifeng and Henan pass to the Mongols.
1233: the Song ally with the Mongols against the Jin.
9 February 1234: the Mongol-Jin war ends at Caizhou.
1234: the Jin end and with them the Goryeo tribute.
9 February 1234: Aizong hangs himself at Caizhou.

wars.name: Jin conquest of the Liao
wars.outcome: Ningjiangzhou and Chuhedian (1114), Huanglong (1115), the five capitals (1120-1122) and Emperor Tianzuo (26 March 1125); the Song took Yanjing from the Jin in May 1123 and lost it in 1125.

wars.name: Jin-Song wars (Jingkang)
wars.outcome: Hebei and Shanxi taken in 1126, Kaifeng on 9 January 1127; the Jin puppets Chu (1127) and Qi (1130-1137); the raid on the Yangtze delta of December 1129-February 1130; Henan and Shaanxi returned in 1139 and retaken in 1140; the Treaty of Shaoxing (ratified 11…

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1161
wars.outcome: Wanyan Liang's invasion crossed the Huai on 28 October 1161, lost at Tangdao and Caishi and ended with his murder on 15 December; the Treaty of Longxing, 1165.

wars.name: Jin-Song war of 1206-1208
wars.outcome: The Song declared war on 14 June 1206 and lost; peace on 2 November 1208 with the Song tribute reinstated.

wars.name: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
wars.outcome: Invasion of 1211, Khitan revolt 1212, the move to Kaifeng 1214, Zhongdu 1 June 1215, Mukhali's clearing of Hebei, Shanxi and Shandong 1217-1223, Shaanxi 1230-1231, Sanfengshan 1232, Kaifeng 1232-1233 and Caizhou on 9 February 1234.

wars.name: Jin-Xia relations and the war of 1210
wars.outcome: Xia attacked the Jin in 1210 after submitting to the Mongols and joined them against the Jin in 1211; Xuanzong 'severed ties' with Western Xia (undated).

certainty.note: The conquest fronts of 1115-1125 and the moving Yellow River-Huai front are approximate.
The Huai-Qinling border with the Song was fixed by the Treaty of Shaoxing (ratified 11 October 1142) and renewed in 1165 and 1208; the northern and western frontiers stay soft.
The Mongol war front changed year by year; the 1223, 1231 and 1233 shapes are approximate.

sources.title: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty
